answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales. Consider a harbor as the anchor of the cost.
